title: Chocolate Hearts Box

adjustment.analysis: No events, promotions, or price changes in the target week. The baseline already reflects recent trends and seasonal patterns. The Valentine's Day spike (2/9: x5.5 vs baseline) and Easter (3/30: x0.6 vs baseline) are accounted for in the model's learning. Past promotions show no reliable lift (noise-adjusted x1.0), and the classical uplift model confirms no expected effect. The median remains at 10.7. The 58% ordinary week noise justifies no adjustment. No drivers justify moving the median or widening spreads.

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-58% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
